entry.title: Working Together to Respond When Disaster Strikes

media:group.media:title: Working Together to Respond When Disaster Strikes
media:group.media:description: When disaster strikes, every second matters. That’s where Texas A&M’s innovative technology, CLARKE, steps in. Using artificial intelligence and drone imagery, CLARKE evaluates damage to infrastructure in just minutes. Responders quickly know which homes and roads are safe or destroyed, giving them life-saving information fast and even mapping safe routes around blocked areas. In this video, you’ll see CLARKE in action after disaster strikes, helping responders quickly assess damage and map safe routes so communities can recover faster, even in hard-to-reach places. This is the future of disaster response powered by Texas A&M’s commitment to serve as a force for good. Read more: https://tx.ag/b9iKhkv

media:group.media:title: Texas A&M Researchers are Working to Prevent Disasters in Cyberspace

That’s why Dr. Nitesh Saxena, professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Texas A&M and associate director of The Global Cyber Research Institute, is working on finding ways to help protect against cyberattacks that could negatively impact disaster recovery. entry.title: Texas A&M at Fast Company's Innovation Festival | Beyond the Moon: The Next Era of Space Innovation

media:group.media:title: Texas A&M at Fast Company's Innovation Festival | Beyond the Moon: The Next Era of Space Innovation
media:group.media:description: Artemis II sent humans farther from Earth than ever before, putting next-generation communications, navigation, spacecraft controls and life-support systems to the ultimate test. But this historic mission is only the beginning. In this panel from the Fast Company Innovation Festival, Texas A&M former students from NASA take us inside the breakthroughs, high-stakes engineering challenges and bold ideas shaping the next era of space exploration. They reveal how Artemis II and emerging commercial space technologies are laying the groundwork for a lasting human presence on the Moon, future missions to Mars, and innovations that could ultimately change life here on Earth.

entry.title: Texas A&M Wins a Fast Company 2026 Innovation by Design Award

media:group.media:title: Texas A&M Wins a Fast Company 2026 Innovation by Design Award
media:group.media:description:
For the second year in a row, Fast Company has recognized Texas A&M University for innovation that makes a difference.
This year's recognition highlights a breakthrough in early dementia detection: an AI-powered Digital Human designed to help identify early signs of dementia through conversational screening, speech cues, facial expression analysis and biometric monitoring. Led by Dr. Mark Benden and supported through Texas A&M's Dementia and Alzheimer's Research Initiative (DARI), the empathetically designed virtual agent helps bridge critical gaps in access to care for rural and underserved communities.
This innovation reflects Texas A&M's commitment to public service and to strengthening the health of communities across Texas, the nation and beyond.
🔗: https://tx.ag/Innovation26

entry.title: Working Together for the Good of America | Texas A&M at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix

media:group.media:title: Working Together for the Good of America | Texas A&M at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix
media:group.media:description:
This year, as America turns 250 and Texas A&M turns 150, Aggies had a visible presence at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C.
Surrounded by monuments and memorials to what generations have built, defended and advanced together, Aggies brought a powerful message to a national stage:
We are working together for the good of America.
From the custom Texas A&M-branded IndyCar driven by Indy 500 champion Felix Rosenqvist, to the national broadcast debut of our 2026 brand anthem on FOX featuring Grammy Award-winning former student Lyle Lovett's cover of "Let's Work Together" — that message resonated across the nation.
What we can do together is far greater than what any one of us can do alone. Together, we stand as a force for good.

entry.title: How Texas A&M's Hagler Institute Attracts World-Class Minds to College Station

media:group.media:title: How Texas A&M's Hagler Institute Attracts World-Class Minds to College Station
media:group.media:description: The Hagler Institute for Advanced Study at Texas A&M University has quietly become one of the most powerful engines for research collaboration in American higher education. Since 2011, it has brought 161 world-class researchers to campus — including six Nobel laureates, an Academy Award winner and a four-time Grammy Award winner — pairing them with rising faculty and graduate students in a unique "triad" model designed to ignite innovation and elevate the next generation of scholars. A bold idea that started 15 years ago has transformed into an institute that has helped grow the university's research funding from $500 million to $1.4 billion, dramatically increased its National Academy members and convinced over 20% of visiting fellows to join the permanent faculty.
